description: Agent-based project dealing with a web portal to displaced and ask questions about fire safety.
summary:
FlameScope is an AI-powered web dashboard that turns NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) combustion archive into ranked, cited fire-safety answers for the lunar habitat era.

We curated all 24 PSI combustion investigations, including 2,003 individual test runs taken directly from PSI's experimental tables, with every fact linked to its source. FlameScope ranks investigations by relevance to habitat safety, modeling and fire-safety equipment, with user-adjustable weights and the evidence behind every score. Its Scenario Lab lets an engineer enter a target atmosphere, such as 34% oxygen at 8.2 psi, and returns the closest real tests, shows where the data stops, and openly bounds the partial-gravity gap rather than inventing numbers. Users can export model-ready data with provenance, browse findings grouped by detection, suppression and material screening, see Earth applications, and ask questions answered only with cited sources.

This matters because future habitats will run at elevated oxygen and reduced pressure, where materials burn more readily, yet decades of microgravity fire research are hard to find and apply. FlameScope gives designers trustworthy, sourced evidence in minutes.
details:
PROJECT DETAILS - FLAMESCOPE

WHAT IT DOES AND HOW IT WORKS

FlameScope is a web dashboard that turns NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) combustion archive into ranked, cited fire-safety answers. We curated all 24 PSI combustion investigations from PSI's public data service: objectives, fuels, hardware, 355 publications, 40 categorized findings and 2,003 individual test runs taken row by row from PSI's experimental tables. Every fact carries a link to its source, and unknown values stay empty rather than guessed.

A batch ingestion pipeline, run once ahead of use, parses this material, rates each investigation against a 15-criterion rubric (habitat relevance, modeling value, and value for fire-safety controls), and indexes the text for search. At request time the dashboard offers ten views:

- Ranking: transparent, adjustable scores with the evidence behind every rating, plus presets such as "lunar habitat" and "equipment designer".

- Scenario Lab: enter an atmosphere (oxygen, pressure, airflow, gravity, fuel) and get the closest real tests, which dimensions the data covers, and an honest statement of the partial-gravity gap, bounded by 0 g and 1 g results instead of invented values.

- Data Extract: model-ready CSV or JSON tables of test runs with provenance columns.

- Safety Tech: findings grouped by detection, suppression, material screening, post-fire hazards and atmosphere design.

- Compare, Explorer, Earth Apps, Ask (cited question answering), an Overview, and an Architecture page that shows how the system itself works.

Ranking, matching and export are deterministic arithmetic. AI is used at request time in only three places (Ask, comparison narratives, scenario explanations), and a citation checker removes any sentence its sources do not support.

BENEFITS

- Finds the evidence relevant to a specific habitat atmosphere in minutes.

- Every number and sentence can be traced back to PSI or a NASA report.

- Scores are explainable and tunable, not a black box.

- Gaps in the data are shown, not hidden.

- Runs on a single laptop. Ranking, matching, export and browsing never need the network. The three AI features use whichever model is configured: a hosted model for the strongest answers, a local model when offline, or a built-in deterministic mode used for testing.

INTENDED IMPACT

Future lunar and Mars habitats are expected to use oxygen-enriched, reduced-pressure air, where materials burn more readily. FlameScope helps habitat and spacecraft engineers choose evidence for that design space, gives modelers real data to validate fire models, points equipment designers to detection and suppression research, and highlights benefits for fire safety on Earth, such as smoke detection.

TOOLS, LANGUAGES, HARDWARE AND SOFTWARE USED

- Languages: Python 3.12, TypeScript, SQL.

- Frontend: Next.js (App Router), React, Tailwind CSS, TanStack Query, Recharts, React Flow, Mermaid.

- Backend: FastAPI, Pydantic, SQLAlchemy, Alembic.

- Data: PostgreSQL 16 with pgvector for combined keyword and semantic search.

- AI: Google Agent Development Kit (ADK) agents running on Ollama (local or hosted models), with nomic-embed-text embeddings and a deterministic mock provider for offline use and testing.

- Data sources: the NASA PSI public data service and experimental tables, the NASA Technical Reports Server (NTRS), and NASA web pages.

- Delivery: Docker and Docker Compose driven by a single Makefile, with an optional Helm chart for Kubernetes.

- Quality: pytest, Vitest, Playwright, axe-core accessibility checks, ruff, mypy, ESLint, and complexity limits. 1,716 automated tests pass across unit, integration and end-to-end levels.

- Hardware: an Apple Silicon Mac laptop.

HOW IT IS CREATIVE

- It treats honesty as a feature: partial gravity is bounded, never interpolated, and AI sentences without support are deleted before anyone sees them.

- AI does the heavy reading once, ahead of time, so the live dashboard stays fast and reproducible.

- The architecture is part of the product, with an interactive page of live diagrams and call flows.

- Engineers can test their own atmosphere instead of reading through decades of reports.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

- Trust and provenance: no fact without a source.

- Data scale: the archive is about 12 TB, so we curate metadata and test tables and link to raw files instead of downloading them.

- Determinism and offline operation for demos and testing.

- Accessibility (WCAG AA contrast, keyboard use, meaning never shown by colour alone).

- Performance (responses under 300 ms).

- Reproducibility: one command to build, deploy, test and tear down.

- Keeping the design written down and enforced by tests as the project grew.
